styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Duomo, La Scala and the Sforza castle.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Leonardo's Last Supper and the Brera galleries.

stays.why: Steps from the cathedral, metro hub and shopping. Noisiest and priciest, but you walk to everything.
Quiet cobbled lanes, the Pinacoteca and good restaurants. Central and walkable.
Canals, aperitivo bars and nightlife. Livelier and cheaper; 20–25 minutes' walk to the Duomo.
Modern towers, Bosco Verticale and easy metro links. Good value near the station.

food: Try risotto alla milanese (saffron rice) and cotoletta, a breaded veal cutlet.
Aperitivo is a Milan ritual: a drink around €8–12 often comes with a buffet of snacks, roughly 6–9pm.
Panzerotti and pizza slices are cheap eats, about €3–6. Busy bakeries mean fresh food.
Book the Last Supper and popular trattorias ahead; many good spots fill up days in advance.
Coffee standing at the bar costs less than sitting at a table. Check the price list.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a Lake Como day trip by train from Milano Centrale; check times and fares on the day.
Design fans can add a half-day at the Triennale design museum and the Porta Nuova towers.
Football lovers: check whether AC Milan or Inter play at San Siro during your dates and book early.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Duomo, the Last Supper and an aperitivo in Navigli; add a night for a Lake Como day trip.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 8°C. Pack a warm coat; museums are quiet.
February: still cold, lows near 2°C. Rain on about 8 days; carry an umbrella.
March: milder, highs around 14°C. Good for walking; expect some rain.
April: pleasant at 18°C. Showers on about 9 days; layers help.
May: warm at 22°C but the wettest month, rain on about 16 days.
June: warm and sunny, highs near 27°C. Long evenings; book sights ahead.
July: hot at 30°C. Sightsee early and late; expect some thunderstorms.
August: hot and often quiet as locals leave. Some restaurants close; check before you go.
September: warm at 24°C and comfortable. A strong month to visit.
October: cooler at 19°C with rain on about 11 days. Bring a jacket.
November: cool and damp, highs near 12°C, rain on about 11 days.
December: cold at 8°C with festive lights and markets. Pack warm layers.

climate_guide.summary: Northern Italian climate: cold, damp winters and warm to hot summers, with rain spread across the year.

items.title: Best time: April to June, September to October
items.text: Mild days around 18–27°C. Comfortable for walking and sightseeing.

items.title: Summer is hot (July–August)
items.text: Highs near 30°C and humid. Plan indoor sights at midday and go out in the evening.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: May is wettest, with rain on about 16 days. Carry a small umbrella year-round.

items.title: Cold winters (December–February)
items.text: Highs around 8°C and lows near 0°C. A warm coat and layers are essential.

items.title: Summer thunderstorms
items.text: Short, heavy storms are common in July and August. They pass quickly.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobbles; a hat and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Metro and trams for the centre; walk between the Duomo, Brera and Navigli.

modes.text: Lines M1–M5 cover the centre. Tickets cost €2.20 for 90 minutes.
Trams and buses run frequently. Buy tickets at newsagents or by app.
Taxis are metered; queues are long at peak hours and during Fashion Week. Uber works in Milan and ride apps are common for airport runs.
Driving in the centre is restricted (Area C). Use park-and-ride at metro termini.
The centre is flat and walkable. Bike sharing is easy to find.
